title: Digital health convenience can combine sensitive data exposure with recurring billing and exit friction
source_unit: Federal Trade Commission, Utah, and California complaint against Hims & Hers; named federal enforcement case, not a representative patient or customer sample
geography: United States federal and state consumer-protection enforcement; Hims & Hers online telehealth and prescription-subscription service

observations.period: July 29, 2026; FTC and state complaint filed

action_type.value: FTC, Utah, and California lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California

alleged_data_practice.value: sharing consumers' health information with third-party advertising platforms including Meta and Snap despite privacy assurances

alleged_billing_practice.value: charging and enrolling many consumers in prescription treatment subscriptions shortly after intake submission without clearly disclosing the timing

case_status_at_check.unit: FTC legal-library case status checked September 17, 2026

observations.method: Official FTC press release and complaint summary; allegations and filing status are preserved as institutional case facts rather than measured rates of data sharing, billing error, or patient harm.
observations.uncertainty: The complaint does not establish that every consumer's health data was shared, that each charge lacked consent, or that any medical outcome, privacy loss, or household hardship occurred. The case supplies no representative customer denominator or verified remedy.
observations.subgroup: Consumers completing Hims online intake and prescription-subscription flows; the complaint describes conditions and flow variants, not a population estimate.
observations.counterinterpretation: Online intake and recurring refills can reduce access barriers and preserve treatment continuity for some patients. A consumer may knowingly accept a data or billing exchange, and a lawsuit is not a final finding.

observations.period: At least 2019 through early 2025; cancellation and refill mechanisms described in complaint

refill_deadline_allegation.value: refills could be processed before the advertised cadence and consumers allegedly had to cancel before a short deadline to avoid the next charge

cancellation_route_allegation.value: most consumers generally had to contact customer service before online cancellation was introduced in 2023; the FTC alleges the later online button was hidden behind multiple steps

privacy_assurance_allegation.value: privacy representations allegedly conveyed that medical records and sensitive information were accessed only by providers while health information was shared with advertising platforms

observations.method: FTC complaint passages summarized in the official press release and complaint filing; historical dates are allegations about product flows, not current usability measurements.
observations.uncertainty: The public case materials do not provide cancellation completion rates, refund rates, refill denial or treatment interruption rates, account-level ad exposure, or later patient trust and switching outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Users of the company's intake, refill, and cancellation flows; mobile, web, state, and time-period differences require separate review.
observations.counterinterpretation: A multi-step flow may still be completed by some users, and a refill deadline can support medication continuity if clearly understood. Later design changes may alter current exposure; implementation remains open.

observations.period: June 18 through September 10, 2025 complaint dates; FTC FOIA release April 2026 checked September 17, 2026

denominator.unit: released Hims & Hers consumer-complaint records in FTC FOIA workbook

complaint_source_composition.value: 196 BBB CA Oakland; 2 FTC Online Complaints; 1 BBB Scam Tracker; 1 Federal Trade Commission; 3 source fields blank

disposition_provided.unit: released complaint records with a disposition indicator

resolved_disposition.unit: released complaint records marked RESOLVED, with complainant verification stated in the disposition label

answered_not_confirmed_satisfactory.unit: released complaint records marked ANSWERED, including cases where the consumer was not heard from or remained dissatisfied according to the disposition label

administratively_invalid.unit: released complaint records marked ADMIN JUDGED INVALID

disposition_missing.unit: released complaint records without a usable disposition label

geographic_spread.unit: distinct nonblank consumer state codes represented; state is not a population denominator

complaint_response_outcome.value: observed administrative response labels, not verified medical, privacy, financial, or treatment outcomes

observations.method: Aggregate coding of non-text workbook fields only: complaint date, source, state code, disposition, and record status. Raw workbook, narrative comments, names, addresses, contact fields, and other personal data were not retained.
observations.uncertainty: The FOIA release is a selected complaint file, not a representative Hims customer sample. The source composition is highly concentrated in one BBB channel; disposition labels do not establish the underlying allegation, compensation, data deletion, treatment continuity, or durable firm change. Blank fields and redactions limit interpretation.
observations.subgroup: People whose complaints entered the released FTC FOIA file, primarily through BBB CA Oakland; complainants with resolved, answered, invalid, and missing-disposition labels are distinct groups.
observations.counterinterpretation: A verified RESOLVED label may indicate a satisfactory resolution for that complainant without proving broader compliance, while an ANSWERED label can reflect either a response or unresolved dissatisfaction; complaint access and source channel shape who appears in the file.

related_sources.claim: FTC describes the lawsuit, alleged health-data sharing, billing, cancellation, and privacy practices.
Redacted complaint provides the alleged intake, refill, cancellation, and privacy-flow details.
FTC case listing reports the pending case status and matter context.
FTC FOIA page identifies the released Hims & Hers consumer-complaints workbook, its request number, release timing, and file size.
Released workbook supplies coded complaint source, date, geography, disposition, and response-field observations.

boundary: This record adds a named digital-health consumer-power case. It links alleged health-data disclosure, recurring prescription billing, and cancellation friction at the institutional case level, but does not establish actual individual data exposure, unauthorized payment, medical harm, treatment interruption, privacy loss, remedy, trust change, or practical exit. The next test is a lawful account/complaint or implementation ledger preserving notice, consent, refill, cancellation, data-sharing, correction, treatment continuity, relief, and later trust separately.
